reasons: The tests are clearly written, but they depend on stand-in objects rather than real outputs.

terms.meaning: Working a number out again from the underlying data to see whether the stored figure is right.
Total gross effort divided by total effort after removing double-counting.
The fraction of effort that is backed by recorded evidence.
The rule that a block cannot claim more supporting items than it actually cites.
A simple fake object with the fields a check reads, used so the test controls every value.

used_by: pytest (runs the test file directly; no other callers visible)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose and imports
sections.what: Loads the three checks and the report type, and explains that each check must read its numbers from outside the claim it verifies.
sections.why: An earlier issue showed that a check reading the same source as the claim could confirm an error instead of catching it.
sections.watch_out: If the summary object is changed to copy claimed values into the check's inputs, these tests may still pass while real code is wrong.

sections.name: Band
sections.title: Effort band stand-in
sections.what: A simple object holding one base effort figure.
sections.why: Rows carry effort figures, and these tests only need the base value.
sections.watch_out: Only the base figure is modelled, so the low and high ranges are not tested here.

sections.name: Row
sections.title: Process row stand-in
sections.what: A simple object for one process row, holding an identifier and three effort figures: released, credited, and realised.
sections.why: The totals checks add these figures up.
sections.watch_out: The field names must match what the checks read, or the tests fail for the wrong reason.

sections.name: Value
sections.title: Summary stand-in
sections.what: A simple summary object whose totals are calculated from the rows unless the test overrides them.
sections.why: Lets a test plant a wrong total or ratio while keeping the rest consistent.
sections.watch_out: This object does no consistency checking of its own, so it is not a model of real data.

sections.name: rows
sections.title: Sample rows
sections.what: Provides two fixed sample rows whose totals are used throughout the tests.
sections.why: Fixed inputs make the expected results easy to reason about.
sections.watch_out: Several assertions quote numbers from these rows, so changing them breaks many tests.

sections.name: TestTheTotalsAreCheckedAgainstTheRows
sections.title: Totals checked against rows
sections.what: Checks that consistent totals pass, and that wrong gross totals, wrong deduplicated totals, and wrong ratios fail. The last test confirms the planted ratio really is wrong and that the rows-based check catches it.
sections.why: The ratio case is one the older method could not catch, because it divided two stored totals that agreed with each other.
sections.watch_out: The message-text assertions depend on exact wording in the check.

sections.name: TestTheEvidencedShareIsCheckedAgainstTheRecords
sections.title: Evidenced share checked against records
sections.what: Checks that a headline share matching the records passes, that a mismatched share fails, and that a value row with no matching record raises an error.
sections.why: A missing record must not be read as an unevidenced process, because that would make the share look smaller and pass wrongly.
sections.watch_out: The error test expects a KeyError whose message contains the phrase no record. Rewording that message breaks it.

sections.name: TestTheConfidenceFeaturesAreCheckedAgainstThePack
sections.title: Confidence citations checked against the pack
sections.what: Checks that a citation count within the citations that resolve in the evidence pack passes, that a count above them fails, and that a citation absent from the pack does not count.
sections.why: The score check reads the count from the same object as the score, so it cannot see an inflated count. This check reads the pack instead.
sections.watch_out: The record is a built fake with most fields empty. If the check begins reading another field, these tests may fail with an unclear error.

summary: Feeds the recomputation checks inconsistent data on purpose and confirms each check catches the error.
purpose: Tests three checks: the totals check, the evidenced-share check, and the confidence-feature check.
why: A check that reads its numbers from the same place as the claim it is checking can never see the error. The tests make sure each check reads its numbers from somewhere independent.
how: Each test builds a summary object or record with one planted inconsistency, runs one check, and asserts the check failed with the expected message. Control tests confirm that consistent data passes.
inputs: Hand-built rows, summary objects, and record objects defined in the test file.
outputs: Pass or fail results from pytest. The file writes no files.
risks: The summary stand-in does not enforce consistency itself, so the tests show the checks work but not that the real producer is consistent. The record stand-ins hold only some fields.
debug: If a totals test fails, compare the planted numbers with the sums the check computes. If a record test fails with an unclear error, check whether the check started reading a field the stand-in lacks.
